notes.title: Individual Soldiers Mode Shows the True Scale of Battles
notes.content: [p][b]Hi everyone,[/b][/p][p]I wanted to share what I’ve been working on these last weeks. One of the most unique aspects of [i]Carthage: Bellum Punicum[/i] is its visual style, where military units are represented with square symbols, the same style you may know from the [i]HistoryMarche[/i] channel, which has been a big inspiration for this project.[/p][p]That said, I thought it could be interesting to also let you see the battles in another way: with all the individual soldiers on the field. This gives a much clearer sense of the scale of the conflict. The largest battles can reach up to 300,000 soldiers on screen, and the engine is capable of supporting up to one million if needed.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/bdce30faea846fcf71d6d82ae434be8df4bc9a0e.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/f09a1e10f6c6cafb8f28f18dbeabab9da0e79d70.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/0722a06a476773a70c4cf7b28bf59ac6b94f415a.gif"][/img][/p][p]Each unit displays the exact number of troops it contains: infantry with 484, cavalry with 256, and foot skirmishers with 361. In this view you can also notice the effect of the "organization" stat, which represents how well the soldiers inside a unit are arranged and disciplined.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/0a89c62c6c6fcaa9c7c128aa1babc9c5281ed980.png"][/img][/p][p]Each individual casualty is shown too, so as the battle unfolds you can actually see soldiers falling and formations thinning out, which makes the clashes feel much more alive and true to the scale of ancient warfare.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/5cc3a258c7fa1c3deedb34b286ea484497b7e1c6.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]I hope you enjoyed it, have a great day everyone![/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/3b656cebafa95c005b4ce48296b2bb4db588f35a.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/a6ff3286df18c15106a72a86237371aaf391911e.gif"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Iberian Map Expansion and Two New Factions Added
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey everyone,[/b][/p][p]Just dropping by to share some progress! This time, I focused on improving the campaign map for Iberia and adding two new Iberian factions.[/p][p]Let’s start with the map. I added 78 new settlements across Iberia, corrected some settlement names to better match their historical counterparts, and included more rivers and roads to give the region a bit more life. Also made some tweaks to the mountains so they blend in better with the rest of the terrain.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/70910e34010b65a7eb9187917310605f71b3f011.png"][/img]

Both were under strong Carthaginian influence at the time, but they still held some independent territories. You'll see that reflected in how they appear on the map—tied to Carthage, but not entirely absorbed by it.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/70910e34010b65a7eb9187917310605f71b3f011.png"][/img]

More to come soon![/b][/p]

notes.title: Commanders, Cultures & Logistics
notes.content: [p]I’ve been working on portraits for generals and commanders. Each faction belongs to a culture group, and every culture has its own unique portrait style. In some cases, like the Celtiberians, a faction belongs to two culture groups, which affects which portrait sets are available to them.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/0a89b14f7396e249fda55631d0ca6183a09f445c.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/3f8d0b67bf001580920fb890ab9b0f70ccd72687.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/290df41c5b3fad19260e2224fad5eaf77b577969.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/a51ee75b7a48920883aa0440df6cd35ce8858d78.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/0e0181af50411c015ea7d7da9afab0eab5e2cc86.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Now on to the economy. Each province has a capital and a few smaller settlements. The smaller ones send their resources to the capital, which then distributes them as needed: like sending iron to blacksmiths or food to settlements that don’t produce any.[/p][p]What’s left after covering all needs stays in the provincial capital as surplus. That surplus is then sent to the faction capital. This makes logistics a key part of the campaign. You’ll be able to intercept large convoys carrying important resources or even cut off supply routes entirely.[/p][p]Every settlement consumes food. If they don’t get enough, they might lose population due to emigration, switch to food production at the cost of output, or even suffer starvation.[/p][previewyoutube="c-E1MClJ0ro;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Units, Equipment & Dynamic Borders
notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/3cd687f88bb2884a04b46113344aa94033693845.png"][/img][/p][p]The game grows every day, but I wanted to share some of the most visible progress. First up: units, their equipment, and their unit cards. You’ll be able to equip units with all kinds of gear—melee weapons like swords, spears, axes, and maces; ranged weapons like bows, slings, and javelins; plus armor, helmets, shields, and mounts. Each piece has its own strengths and weaknesses, and every item shows up on the unit card so you can see exactly what they’re carrying. This means endless combinations.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/72beea450a8961945e5ca415bf5d3fe557f623ba.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Also, I’ve been working on dynamic borders for the campaign map. Strategy players love painting the whole map in their faction’s color. I’m one of them. Most games have fixed borders, but I wanted something better. Something that makes it satisfying to see your army push into enemy lands. So I made dynamic borders. Every settlement, from small villages to big cities, has its own territorial influence. Armies also create influence while on the move.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="7YVpLZOuGns;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]Hope you like these updates![/b][/p]

notes.title: Geronium Battle Map Reveal
notes.content:
Today I’m excited to share the Geronium battle map as it appears in [b]Carthage: Bellum Punicum[/b], alongside a comparison with the historical illustration from [i]Ancient Battlefields: Building Blocks for an Ancient War History (Volume 3)[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45505500/ae9fbb52ebbe61560cd1cdec8c9e8f34f00064f4.jpg[/img]
This is part of my ongoing effort to faithfully recreate historical settings while ensuring they work well for gameplay.

I keep working hard every day on the game. My main focus right now is building and polishing battles, aiming to start internal testing as soon as possible. A big part of this is the battle AI—I’ll do my best to make it the best ever seen in any strategy game.

Thanks for following the development and taking the time to read this update—your support means a lot!
